page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are dedicated rather than shared, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES. The instance contains 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation ratio. It has no bundled local instance storage and relies on network-attached block devices, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computing throughput offset by reliable memory capacity. CPU performance tests place the instance in the lower percentiles, recording a single-core score of 969.0 and a multi-core score of 3819.0 in Geekbench, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 6967.25. Memory bandwidth reaches 41.01 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 35.87 GB/sec for writes, both falling within median cloud benchmarks. In data processing workloads, it executes 5.58 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves 5.86 GB/sec in static web throughput. Small-scale model inference achieves 457.92 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M parameter model, though generation drops to 5.25 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

From an infrastructure perspective, the ecs.r5.2xlarge balances substantial memory allocation against moderate compute performance. The lack of integrated NVMe storage requires external disk provisioning for persistent storage needs, and the 2 Gbps baseline network caps maximum data ingest rates. This instance configuration is suitable for memory-intensive caching tiers, small-to-medium in-memory databases, data transformation pipelines, and backend application servers requiring high RAM capacity without intense CPU core demands.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, supported by 64.0 GB of system memory, offering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX-512, VNNI, and AES. It provides no local ephemeral storage, utilizing network storage instead, and delivers a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic benchmarks reveal moderate memory bandwidth alongside lower-tier single-thread and multi-thread compute performance, logging 3819.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 5.58 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. This hardware configuration fits memory-heavy workloads, such as Redis or Memcached instances, mid-sized relational database hosting, and memory-bound ETL processing.
